title: Automation Intake → AI Scoping → Triage → Spec & Runbook

sections.label: 1 · INTAKE
sections.note: Every automation request enters one door in one shape. Ad-hoc requests in DMs are why automation backlogs become folklore.

sections.label: 2 · SCOPE
sections.note: The agent checks what the request actually touches — which systems, whether the APIs exist, where the data has to transform — before anyone estimates it.

sections.label: 3 · TRIAGE
sections.note: A written yes or a written no. Parking a request with a reason is what stops the same idea being re-proposed every quarter.

sections.label: 4 · SPEC & RUNBOOK
sections.note: Nothing is built from a conversation. The spec and the runbook are generated together, so the documentation cannot drift from what shipped.

nodes.label: APIs exist and the payback is under 90 days

nodes.notes: A typed spec, not hand-written node JSON — an invalid node type becomes impossible rather than merely unlikely.
